extracted.intended_audience: customers, media, general public, affected stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A short public statement issued by a company's CEO in response to a high-profile incident, intended to acknowledge the event, apologize, outline corrective actions, and reassure stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge the event clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Open by naming or characterizing the incident so the audience knows what statement refers to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language from page: "The truly horrific event that occurred on this flight has elicited many responses..." Use an explicit acknowledgement (describe or label the incident) rather than burying or ignoring it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer a direct apology
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an explicit, personal apology to those harmed or affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page wording: "my deepest apologies for what happened... I deeply apologize to the customer forcibly removed and to all the customers aboard." Prefer first-person apologies ('I apologize') rather than indirect or passive constructions ('mistakes were made').

rubrics_metrics.name: Express empathy and shared sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate that leadership shares the audience's feelings (e.g., outrage, anger, disappointment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the statement: "I share all of those sentiments, and one above all... Like you, I continue to be disturbed by what happened..." Use empathetic language to validate stakeholders' reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state that the organization takes responsibility for the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page: "I want you to know that we take full responsibility and we will work to make it right." A clear admission of responsibility avoids deflection and signals accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: Promise concrete efforts to fix the underlying problems that led to the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "we are going to fix what's broken" and "I have committed to our customers and our employees that we are going to fix what’s broken so this never happens again." Statements should go beyond regret to commitment to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: List specific areas/processes for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify particular policies, procedures, or partnerships that will be examined or changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page enumerates: "a thorough review of crew movement, our policies for incentivizing volunteers in these situations, how we handle oversold situations and an examination of how we partner with airport authorities and local law enforcement." Specific items help signal seriousness and give audiences measurable targets to watch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a concrete timeline for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: State when the organization will report back or complete the review/actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the release: "We'll communicate the results of our review by April 30th." Giving a date creates accountability and reduces speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassure commitment to improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Close with a promise to do better and restore trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example closing: "I promise you we will do better." Use concise, affirmative language to reassure stakeholders about future behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address affected parties explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Name or reference the people harmed or impacted and direct the apology to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page: "I deeply apologize to the customer forcibly removed and to all the customers aboard." Calling out victims or affected groups demonstrates recognition of harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use moral/ethical language to condemn mistreatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include normative statements that condemn the inappropriate behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the text: "No one should ever be mistreated this way." Moral language helps frame the incident as unacceptable and justifies corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior-leader authorship and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the statement come from a named senior executive and include a closing/signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Header and sign-off on page: "Statement from United Airlines CEO Oscar Munoz" and "Sincerely, Oscar." Leadership attribution increases credibility and signals that the matter is taken at the highest level.
